pll2d12c6-d1e3519.summary: Cites Alcuin: God works in four ways: first, disposing all in the Word; second, creating the unformed matter of the four elements from nothing ('he created all things together'); third, distinguishing creatures in the six days; fourth, renewing known natures from primordial seeds so they do not perish.
claims: All bodies were created materially at once.

pl-l2d12c6.summary: Gives Alcuin's four modes of divine working: disposing all in the Word; creating the unformed matter of the four elements from nothing ('he created all things together'); distinguishing creatures through the six days' works; and continually renewing known natures from primordial seeds so they do not perish.
claims: God works in four ways: disposing in the Word, creating matter from nothing, distinguishing in six days, and renewing natures from seeds.
All elements were created materially at once.
Known natures are renewed from primordial seeds, not new ones created.
